safety_lead_time.comparison_action: increase safety lead time from 2.5 to 2.34 days (marginal adjustment)

narrative: Material PL1__M0A4C270 exhibits intermittent demand with high variability (CV=1.26) and very short but unpredictable lead times (mean 0.77 days, CV=1.17). The current SAP safety stock of 396 units provides only approximately 75% service level, far below the 95% target. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with safety stock raised to 778 units and a reorder point of 1,034 units is recommended to close this service level gap at a modest incremental annual cost of ~$690.
warnings: Recommended safety stock is 96% higher than SAP baseline — ERP update required
High demand variability (CV=1.26) — monitor and improve forecast accuracy
High lead time variability (CV=1.17) — consider supplier reliability improvement programs

research_insights.selection_rationale: Continuous review is appropriate given moderately high daily demand, short variable lead times, and the need to tightly control stockout exposure. The fixed-order-quantity EOQ minimises total ordering and holding costs while the reorder point provides the service level buffer. This model maps directly to SAP MRP reorder point logic.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity does not bind: peak inventory (778 SS + 2190 OQ = 2,968 units) is 21% below the 3,764-unit maximum. No capacity-driven order quantity reduction was required.
